issue.title: The router cache does not operate properly

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

issue.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/doinki/next-route-cache

### To Reproduce

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm start
```

The first dynamic page is cached, and after 30 seconds, requests continue to be sent without being cached.
After 30 seconds, you can see that the date changes every time you visit the dynamic page.

![1](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/90969158/738dd341-c405-419f-8dc5-a1f02a1a0b2c)

<video src='https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/90969158/ec88f2b6-c438-415c-a86b-71e4270f9f20'></video>



### Current vs. Expected behavior

## Current
After 30 seconds, the router cache does not work.

## Expected behavior
If you visit the dynamic page again after 30 seconds, it should be cached for 30 seconds.

### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 23.1.0: Mon Oct  9 21:27:24 PDT 2023; root:xnu-10002.41.9~6/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
Binaries:
  Node: 20.10.0
  npm: 10.2.3
  Yarn: 1.22.19
  pnpm: 8.12.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 14.0.4
  eslint-config-next: 14.0.4
  react: 18.2.0
  react-dom: 18.2.0
  typescript: 5.3.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```


### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

App Router

### Additional context

_No response_

body:
There seems to be an issue when the `prefetch` of the `<Link />` component is not set.

To be precise, the problem seems to be when the state of `PrefetchKind` is `auto`. The logic in the prefetch reducer that updates the `lastUsedTime` and `prefetchTime` by setting the value of `state.prefetchCache` throughout the code is only in the prefetch reducer. However, when in `auto` mode, the conditional does not reach the prefetch action in the Link component.

Therefore, from 30 seconds to 5 minutes after the first update within the navigate action, i.e. the navigate reducer, which is triggered on the click event of the `<Link />` component, the `getPrefetchEntryCacheStatus()` value is evaluated to `PrefetchCacheEntryStatus.stale`, and it is continuously refetched, and only after 5 minutes does it become `PrefetchCacheEntryStatus.exipired` and a new `state.prefetchCache` is assigned.

This is a wrong action and I think we need some logic to update the `prefetchTime` once the cache with the `PrefetchCacheEntryStatus.stale` value is used.

Of course, this can be solved with `<Link prefetch={true} />`, but that's not possible in a development environment, and I'm actually having [this difficulty](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/60279) because of the stale refetch method.
 
If I'm having trouble because I'm using Next.js in a way it wasn't intended, I'd like some solid guidelines.

Thanks for the explanation!
I have already worked on this issue in #58997 and successfully fixed it by updating the `lastUsedTime`. I think this is simpler than adding a reducer, but I am not sure if updating the `lastUsedTime` is justified by design.

issue.title: Renew prefetch cache entry after update from server
issue.body:
### What
When a prefetch cache entry becomes "stale", it'll remain stale until eventually it gets evicted. However during that stale window, the cache is never revalidated, and so instant navigations stop working and data is fetched from origin every navigation.

### Why
The `lastUsedTime` entry on the prefetch cache is currently only updated after the first read. Once it becomes stale, `applyFlightData`'s recursive functions will see that there is no longer a reusable prefetch cache entry, and will trigger a lazy fetch of the new data on every subsequent navigation. 

### How
This updates prefetch cache handling to always ensure we’re using a fresh or reusable prefetch cache entry. This means that stale prefetch entries will be refreshed on a navigation event. As a result of this, I’ve had to disable one of our tests that relies on this stale cache behavior. It’s not ideal that we’re blocked on the loading boundary when fetching child segment data—ideally we can refactor this to cache the loading component in the CacheNode and copy it over on navigations, similar to how ‘head’ is handled. I’ll work on this in a separate PR. 

Note: The new client cache test for this is disabled in PPR for the same reason as the other tests: auto prefetching with PPR navigations is currently loading fresh data rather than reusing the prefetch cache. 


Fixes #58969
Fixes #58723
Closes NEXT-1904
